newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-BENFICA LOSE TO LOWLY BELENENSES, SLIP TO THIRD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENFICA LOSE TO LOWLY BELENENSES, SLIP TO THIRD.

text.p: Benfica lost 2-1 to Belenenses at home on Saturday, their third consecutive defeat, and slipped down to third place in the Portuguese first division.

Sporting beat Boavista 3-1 at home to go second with 34 points, one ahead of Benfica. Reigning champions Porto, who meet Gil Vicente on Monday, look to have the title safely in their grasp with 44 points.
Benfica, who were booed by fans during the game, have been without a coach since Brazilian Paulo Autuori stepped down on Monday and were missing suspended captain Joao Pinto.
Their lack of leadership was obvious from the outset. Belenenses opened the scoring after just five minutes when a header from defender Paulo Fonseca found the net after a cross by Rui Esteves.
Benfica's Colombian defender Jorge Bermudez inadvertently extended Belenenses' lead in the 30th minute with an own goal which shot past keeper Michel Preud'Homme.
Benfica midfielder Bruno Caires brought the score to 2-1 in the 50th minute with a powerful shot inside the box after a corner from Valdo Filho.
But Belenenses' strong defence held out for the rest of the game. Benfica's best chance of an equaliser came in the 68th minute when Romanian midfielder Nica Panduru hit the left post.

Sporting took an early two-goal lead against Boavista's shaky defence. Striker Pedro Barbosa, unmarked in the box, scored from a pass by Ricardo Sa Pinto in the sixth minute and Bulgarian Ivaylo Iordanov got a second six minutes later.
Sporting captain Oceano Cruz then converted a penalty in the 30th minute after Boavista midfielder Jorge Couto fouled defender Luis Pedrosa.
Boavista, who have had a disappointing season and are now in 13th place, got a consolation goal in the 80th minute from a 20-metre freekick by Surinam striker Jerrel Jimmy.
